questions.prompt: Why check out a Vault item before editing it?
questions.explanation: Checkout shows who is editing an item so teammates can coordinate. It is not a hard lock against every possible upload.

answers.text: To show teammates who is editing it so they can coordinate
So officers can approve every change before it's made
To limit how many files are stored in the repository
To track how long each member spends on CAD

questions.prompt: You upload a new version of an item. What happens to the previous one?
questions.explanation: The previous version stays in the Vault history, even after a new check-in becomes the latest. Downloading an older version does not automatically restore it.

answers.text: It's kept in the version history and stops being the current version
It's deleted to save storage
It is copied into the general Files source
It stays current until an officer promotes the new one

questions.prompt: What does an assembly's current BOM show?
questions.explanation: The current BOM links child items, quantities, and optional notes. It does not pin child version IDs.

answers.text: Linked child items and quantities, without pinned child versions
Who has worked on the assembly and for how long
The order in which the parts should be assembled
Which parts are currently checked out

questions.prompt: You need to edit a part that a teammate currently has checked out. What's the right move?
questions.explanation: Talk to them — the lock is visible and it names the holder, which is the point. Uploading a parallel copy outside the Vault recreates exactly the `_FINAL_actual` problem the Vault exists to prevent.

answers.text: Message them — the lock shows who holds it — and wait or agree a hand-off
Work on your own copy and upload it as a separate item
Email the file to them and ask them to merge it
Upload a competing version without contacting the holder

questions.prompt: Where can you link a Vault release proposal to a project task?
questions.explanation: The change-request form has an optional Linked task picker. Item detail does not currently offer a direct task link.

answers.text: In the change-request form's optional Linked task field
Directly from every Vault item detail

questions.prompt: You want a Slack DM whenever someone checks in a new version of one bracket, and nothing about the rest of the Vault. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Watch that item and keep New check-ins on in its chevron menu, then set "New check-in on an item I watch" to Slack DM or Both in Notification preferences. Watches are per item; delivery is per event type. Notices only reach members who can still open the project.

answers.text: Watch the bracket, and set Vault check-ins to Slack DM or Both in Notification preferences
Check the bracket out and leave it checked out so every check-in pings you
Save a search for the bracket's part number; saved views send alerts
Nothing: every project member is messaged about every check-in

questions.prompt: The Changes tab compares two STL versions of a bracket. The geometry diff shows sizes in "model units" and no volume. Why?
questions.explanation: STL files store no length unit, so the diff will not guess one. Declare the unit the files were exported in and it can report physical sizes and, for a closed solid, the volume.

answers.text: STL files carry no unit, and no export unit has been declared yet
The bracket is too small for the diff to measure
Volumes are only shown after a change request is approved
The diff only measures STEP files
